facts.label: The facts of one incident, filled in by code (klaxon.agent.postmortem) from a gated run's saved evidence: its run.json, the gate's request, decision and log, and the loop's trace. Each fact says where it comes from. The incident: a fault injected on purpose into a payments system on one machine, with synthetic data and a simulated provider, so no real money.

run.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
run.what_it_was: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was approved with make approve (the request's id typed at a terminal), and the action ran: redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT dollars -> cents, REFUND_CONNECTION returned (unchanged). Code, not the model, then verified it (klaxon.agent.verify): passed; the cause is removed, and the money is not right. The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-742c) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.

timeline.what: The alert rules were quiet at 2 evaluations in a row, and the money check passed: the stack was ready for the fault.

The fault's injection began, on purpose (klaxon.faults): a deploy of payments-api with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It took 2.4 s. The deploy log has it as deploy 21, by klaxon.faults, at 2026-10-24T08:27:03Z.
The alert MoneyCheckFailed fired, raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed: The money check failed 1 of its 5 invariants: payments_match_provider (56 findings).

Klaxon's loop began to investigate the alert: claude-opus-5-5 through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, with read-only tools, offered one write action (rollback_deploy) that runs only if a person approves it.
The loop stopped: diagnosed (confidence 0.85), after 6 steps and 5 tool calls, in 32.5 s.
The money check right before the request: 149 payments that disagree with the provider's charges.

Klaxon asked to act, at the approval gate: request r-742c, redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT dollars -> cents, REFUND_CONNECTION returned (unchanged). It was open until 2026-10-24T08:37:52Z. Its undo: going back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars would deploy a known-bad setting: Klaxon will not; a person can, by hand.
Request r-742c was approved with make approve: typed at a terminal.
The action ran: deploy 22 of payments-api in the deploy log, by Klaxon, approved request r-742c, with PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned.
The money check right after the action: 1080 payments that disagree with the provider's charges.
Health, by code: 2 rounds of the rules and the containers, from 2026-10-24T08:33:19Z to 2026-10-24T08:33:35Z: healthy.
The later money check, at least a minute after the action: 1080 payments that disagree with the provider's charges.
Verification, by code and not by the model: passed.

The harness's clearing, its safety net, asked for the good settings of payments-api (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned). The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-742c) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.
The rules read the stack again after the clearing: the alert MoneyCheckFailed fired; the money check failed: payments_match_provider 1080.

model_words.note: the loop's own words, from a model: data, not checked by code
model_words.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 08:27:01Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Since then it sends our amount in cents to fake-provider as if it were dollars, so the provider charges 100x what we recorded. The first affected payment is pmt_000230: we recorded 1291 cents and the provider charged 129100. Every payment after the deploy is overcharged this way, which produces the payments_match_provider findings. The ledger books what the provider reports, so the ledger still matches the provider and stays balanced, but customers are overcharged against our records.
model_words.fix_summary: Roll payments-api back to the settings it ran before the 08:27:01Z deploy, presumably CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents. That stops new 100x charges. Afterwards, refund the overcharged difference for pmt_000230 onward, or the full charge if refunding and re-charging is simpler, and correct the ledger. Check pmt_000233, which is pending on our side but charged at the provider, and settle its status.
model_words.blast_radius: Recreating payments-api pauses payment and refund intake for a few seconds. Requests in flight during the restart may fail and be retried under their idempotency keys. The rollback repairs nothing: the roughly 63 overcharged payments stay wrong until a separate repair. The previous settings are not shown in c2, so the rollback assumes the earlier value was cents.
model_words.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy payments-api with the settings from the 08:27:01Z deploy (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned). Then run money_check again to confirm that new payments match the provider.

narrative.summary: On 2026-10-24 a fault was injected on purpose into a payments system running on one machine, with synthetic data and a simulated provider, so no real money moved. The fault was a deploy of payments-api with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It made the provider charge customers 100 times the amount our records kept. The alert MoneyCheckFailed fired 17.4 s after the fault. Klaxon investigated and named the cause, and the grading rule agreed. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to redeploy payments-api with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents. The request r-742c was approved, and the action ran as deploy 22. Verification by code passed. The cause was removed and the stack was healthy, but the money was not right. The last money check still found 1080 payments that disagreed with the provider's charges. That damage stays until a person repairs it.
narrative.timeline: At 08:27:00 UTC the alert rules were quiet at 2 evaluations in a row, and the money check passed. The fault's injection then began. The deploy log has it as deploy 21 of payments-api, by klaxon.faults, at 08:27:03 UTC, and it took 2.4 s. At 08:27:18 UTC the alert MoneyCheckFailed fired. At 08:27:19 UTC Klaxon's loop began to investigate. At 08:27:51 UTC the loop stopped on diagnosed, after 6 steps and 5 tool calls, in 32.5 s. At 08:27:52 UTC Klaxon made request r-742c at the gate, open until 08:37:52 UTC. It was approved at 08:33:15 UTC, after 323 s. The action ran at 08:33:18 UTC as deploy 22. Health checks ran from 08:33:19 UTC to 08:33:35 UTC and found the stack healthy. A later money check ran at 08:34:18 UTC. Verification passed at 438.1 s after the fault. The harness's clearing followed at 438.3 s, found the good settings already running, and changed nothing. At 08:35:49 UTC the rules read the stack again, and MoneyCheckFailed fired.
narrative.impact: At the alert the money check failed 1 of its 5 invariants, payments_match_provider, with 56 findings. Ledger and payment-confirmer lag were 0. Right before the request, 149 payments disagreed with the provider's charges. Of those, 145 had a differing amount, and 4 were pending but charged with a differing amount. Right after the action, 1080 payments disagreed. Of those, 1060 had a differing amount, and 20 were pending but charged with a differing amount. The damage grew while the request waited for approval. The later check at 08:34:18 UTC and the reading after the clearing both still showed 1080. The first examples began at pmt_000230. The synthetic clients sent 3 new payments per second on average. 1791 payments arrived and all 1791 got an answer. 1771 succeeded, 0 were refused, and 20 were left with their outcome unknown and still pending at the client's last status check. Refunds: 167 succeeded and 0 were refused. The clients retried 98 times. The evidence does not say whether the 20 pending payments are the same ones the money check listed as pending but charged.
narrative.cause: The recorded cause was a deploy of the payments API with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It read each amount, already in cents, as dollars and converted it to cents again. So the provider charged every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records kept the right one. The payments then disagreed with the provider's charges, and that failed the payments_match_provider invariant, which raised MoneyCheckFailed. Klaxon's diagnosis, with confidence 0.85, said payments-api had been redeployed with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars and the provider was charging 100 times what we recorded. A rule in klaxon.grading, not a person or a model, judged that it names the cause. It found every required element named, and found that the fix fits the remedy. The rule reads words, not meaning. The diagnosis gave a deploy time that differs from the deploy log's time. It also claimed the ledger still matches the provider, which code did not check.
narrative.response: Klaxon had tools that only read, plus one write action, rollback_deploy, which runs only if a person approves it. It asked at the gate, as request r-742c, to redeploy payments-api with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT changed from dollars to cents and the other settings unchanged. The request's undo said going back to dollars would deploy a known-bad setting, which Klaxon will not do, though a person can by hand. The request was approved with make approve, typed at a terminal. The gate's log records how a decision was made, not who made it. The rule is that only Aravind approves. The action ran as deploy 22, with PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents and REFUND_CONNECTION=returned. Verification by code passed. Every container was healthy and the rules were quiet at 2 evaluations in a row. Nothing the provider made after the action was booked wrong, so the cause was removed. The money was not right. The facts do not explain why the alert fired again after the clearing, while verification had found the rules quiet.
narrative.repairs: The last money check, at 08:34:18 UTC, still found 1080 payments that disagree with the provider's charges. A rollback repairs nothing. Repairs that move money are not among Klaxon's actions, so a person must make them. The recorded remedy is to refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider. Our API refunds no more than our recorded amount, so this needs a write with approval. The 20 payments still pending at the client's last status check also need a person's attention. The evidence does not say whether each has settled since. The damaged payments the check lists need the repair the fault records, not a retry or being marked failed.
